Two Intel runs have now failed to find a published f*, and the correct current state of that fact is UNMEASURED rather than negative, because the population never contained a resolvable persistent-state system. There is a third and much cheaper route, proposed as next_question Part B in EXP-INTEL-36306525220 and still not executed, whose evidence is already hash-pinned in this repository. arXiv:2608.05784v1 prints, verbatim in the preserved 69,607-character text layer at research/experiments/EXP-INTEL-36306525220/raw/fulltext/2608.05784v1.txt (sha256 e286167a6ae51eebe1552f655876bae5a9c1728e16793b31e4adac4e9b154dbf): 'E[$/task] = (1-hq) Cmiss p + hq(Chit+Cverify) + h(1-q)Cwrong + Cwrite N , (1) where h is recurrence, q the fraction of hits correctly matched, p the base success rate, N the reuse count, and the C-terms per-branch costs. Every term is already priced in the works above; the one input none of them measures is h on the pre-delegation passive corpus.' Freeze and execute exactly this determination, which needs no new HTTP request, no new corpus, no browser, no Docker and no credential. (a) State the COLD COUNTERFACTUAL arm explicitly as E_cold = Cmiss*p - the same expression with the carried state absent - because the published model prices only the branch an agent actually takes and never prices the alternative, and a break-even is meaningless without the alternative. (b) Derive the per-task saving and the break-even with the algebra shown, f* = Cwrite / (E_cold - E_warm) where E_warm is the Eq. (1) value, and state explicitly which accounting convention is assumed for the printed term Cwrite*N - is the write cost charged once in total, or once per reuse? - because that single convention moves f* by orders of magnitude and the paper does not disambiguate it. This is the accounting-convention discipline this whole lane exists to impose, applied to the paper that supplied the model. (c) Evaluate f* over the paper's own published parameter values - R 60-343x modeled, h 0.090 in-sample and 0.077 out-of-sample, the match-precision term q the paper reports degrading below 1, p the base success rate - and publish the regime table: over which (h, q, Cwrite, Cverify) values is f* finite, what is f* at the published point estimates, and at what h does f* become operationally reachable at all. (d) State the divergence condition explicitly, which is that the carried state never pays for itself when E_cold <= E_warm plus the amortized write cost. TWO DECISIVE AND OPPOSITE OUTCOMES, both decision-grade, neither requiring a single new request. If f* is finite and below an operational bound across the published parameter range, then a measured f* IS reportable in this class, its absence in two Intel runs is a REPORTING-PRACTICE finding, and one properly designed census is worth funding. If f* is divergent, or finite only at values of h that the paper itself declares it never measured, then the persistence-economics anchor is unavailable from this literature class BY CONSTRUCTION - which converts a three-cycle open external search into a bounded structural negative, tells Product that no published f* can ever be borrowed and that SPIDER must measure the marginal recurrence h(N) of carried state against reuse count itself, and identifies h(N) as the very stationarity metric Part B was looking for externally and that Runtime's freshness guard needs.
